Comment: Shrinking baseline of the eleven offending lines at the audited base. One entry per authored line, with its reason and exact decoded text. Do not add exceptions for new wording. Remove an entry in the same change that fixes or removes its line; stale entries fail. Proposed replacements are in docs/design/first-week-island-words.md.

Lines.Text: Save up, then BUY the damaged dory at the Nine Mile Creek shipwright.
Lines.Reason: The old task sends him to the mainland yard; the first dory now belongs at the island slip. Replacement awaits a wording decision.

Lines.Text: At Nine Mile Creek: sell your clams, then buy a COD LICENCE to fish.
Lines.Reason: The old task sends him to the mainland counter; the island licence listing is in draft 1590. Replacement awaits a wording decision.

Lines.Text: Walk the bared sandbar east to Nine Mile Creek before the tide floods it back.
Lines.Reason: The old task sends him across the bar during the island week. Replacement awaits a wording decision.

Lines.Text: Seaworthy at last — sail your dory home to Coddle Cove.
Lines.Reason: The old task sends him away immediately after mending his dory. Replacement awaits a wording decision.

Lines.Text: Then the sandbar to Nine Mile Creek opens up, dry enough to walk. Go before the flood seals it, mind — dawdle and you're stuck till the next low.
Lines.Reason: The opening still directs an early mainland crossing. Replacement awaits a wording decision.

Lines.Text: In Nine Mile Creek, sell your clams, buy a COD LICENCE and a ROD, and save. There's a damaged dory for sale at the shipwright — buy her, pay to put her right, and she's truly yours.
Lines.Reason: The opening still bundles licence, rod and first-dory shopping on the mainland. Replacement awaits a wording decision.

Lines.Text: Then sail her home to Coddle Cove. That's where your harbour starts. Off you go, now — the tide won't wait on us.
Lines.Reason: The opening still sends the repaired first dory away from the island. Replacement awaits a wording decision.

Lines.Text: Back already? Good. Watch the tide — clams on the flats at low water, then the bar to Nine Mile Creek.
Lines.Reason: The repeat greeting still directs an early mainland crossing. Replacement awaits a wording decision.

Lines.Text: And I'll not price my neighbours the way they do over at Nine Mile Creek. A store that squeezes a small place kills it — and then where's the store?
Lines.Reason: A mainland price comparison still names an outside place; the guard covers flavour as well as directions. Replacement awaits a wording decision.

Lines.Text: "So I'll leave you something better than a boat: the way to earn one. Dig clams on the low-water flats. Walk the bar to Nine Mile Creek. Buy a licence, a rod, and a hull worth mending."
Lines.Reason: The letter still directs first-boat shopping over the bar. Replacement awaits a wording decision.

Lines.Text: Signs you off to take cod on rod and line. Written over the counter at LeBlanc's on St Peters, or by the Nine Mile Creek harbourmaster - the same paper either way.
Lines.Reason: The island listing now names LeBlanc's first but still offers the mainland harbourmaster as a second issuer. Replacement awaits a wording decision.
